A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same TD-learning analysis, sharing Algorithm 1 and the central convergence result. Their text, equations, visual material, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated proofs.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical convergence results and proofs, including Appendices A–C, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: Figures 1–2 and Appendix F report original TD(0) simulations on a synthetic 50-state ring MDP, measuring boundedness, divergence, and suboptimality.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 raises the required step-size scale from c > 30 + sqrt(1302) to c >= 281. This changes the permitted parameter range while retaining the linear TD update, initialization, projection-free procedure, and functional form of the decreasing step size.

E1.justification: v2 adds one synthetic policy-evaluation scenario: a 50-state directed-ring MDP with one action. v1 contains no empirical task evaluation. This is a limited addition of synthetic coverage, without broader benchmark or application coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically benchmarks competing learning algorithms. v2's Table 1 compares published theoretical guarantees; its constant-step TD experiment is an internal sensitivity control rather than an added competing baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces a protocol for the toy MDP: gamma = 0.9, five features, T = 10^7, feature rescaling, decreasing and constant step sizes, and a directly solved projected Bellman reference. It defines boundedness, divergence above squared norm 10^12, and suboptimality diagnostics. These are new experimental settings, not revisions to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds a dedicated empirical stability analysis absent from v1. Figure 1 sweeps step-size scale across three feature-conditioning settings; Figure 2 repeats the analysis with constant step sizes to test whether the observed instability requires a time-varying schedule.

E5.justification: Appendix F newly reports 48 independent trajectories per step-size scale and fixed seeds for generating rewards and features. v1 has no corresponding experimental run or seed reporting; this is new reporting, not an established increase over earlier runs.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 add the paper's empirical result set: boundedness, divergence-frequency, and suboptimality curves under both step-size schedules. They show instability for small c, stabilization beyond an empirical threshold, and conditioning-dependent suboptimality. These are newly reported findings, not performance improvements over comparable v1 experiments.

T1.justification: The central proof bounds are substantially revised: the conditional-bias factor changes from 8 to 16, v2 Lemma C.2 corrects per-iterate indexing in the gradient-norm bound, and Theorem D.1 rederives the boundedness constants and horizon condition. Theorem 4.2 explicitly includes reward/feature dependence already present in v1's proof. Lemma 5.1 is retained, with its proof moved to Appendix E.

C1.justification: v2 qualifies the novelty claim specifically as the first projection-free, curvature-independent robust convergence guarantee. v1's contribution sentence claimed the first finite-time unprojected Markovian analysis more broadly. The central self-bounding contribution and O-tilde(1/sqrt(T)) convergence claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting empirical instability to the step-size threshold and suggesting that the robust rate can be pessimistic when curvature is large. It also develops the complementary roles of robust and fast rates. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit non-anytime limitation, although Algorithm 1 still requires the horizon T.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds simulation implementation details, including Julia, ring transition probabilities, reward/feature generation, the direct fixed-point calculation, and a code-access link. v1 provides the mathematical algorithm but no corresponding simulation implementation or code-access information.

R1.justification: The positioning is substantially reorganized around robust versus fast guarantees. Added discussion of Patil et al. (2023) and Samsonov et al. (2024) distinguishes universal step sizes, independent versus Markovian observations, and data dropping. Table 1 consolidates this comparison, while additional citations support the robustness and mixing-time discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and proof exposition are extensively rewritten. Section 4 now separates strong-convexity, projection-based, and proposed arguments. Background material and appendices are reorganized, notation receives a separate appendix, and the curvature proof moves out of the main text.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 1 and two three-by-three experimental figure grids, introducing substantial visual presentation absent from v1. The table summarizes theoretical assumptions and rates; the figures display stability and suboptimality across settings. Equations and surrounding text also reflow with the restructuring.

improvement.justification: v2 more precisely positions its novelty, improves consistency between the main bound and its derivation, corrects gradient-bound indexing, and adds documented experiments illustrating stability. These provide useful gains without extending the central asymptotic result, and the empirical evidence remains confined to one toy MDP. Removing the explicit fixed-horizon limitation partly offsets the improvements.
